name: Integers
summary: The ring of integers modulo m (m at least 2); R!x maps an integer, or a rational with a unit denominator, into it.

examples.code: R := Integers(12); x := R!5; x * 7; x^-1; Order(x); IsUnit(R!4);

differs: Integers(1), the zero ring, is refused.
Order of a residue modulo an m of more than 128 bits is refused.
A collection of residues coerces assignments only when its universe is declared: [R | 1, 7] takes Q[2] := 13, but [R!1, 7] refuses it.
Append and Include of an integer to a collection of residues are refused, even with a declared universe [R | ...] or {R | ...}.

name: Sym
summary: The symmetric group on 1 .. n; G!(1, 2, 3) or G![2, 3, 1] makes a permutation p, and i^p is the image of i.
differs: Iterating over Sym(n) gives its permutations in Sagebrush's own (lexicographic) order, not Magma's.
Only the symmetric and dihedral groups themselves: their subgroups (sub< G | ... >) and other permutation groups are refused.

name: DihedralGroup
summary: The dihedral group of order 2n (n >= 3) as permutations of 1 .. n: G.1 the rotation (1, 2, ..., n), G.2 the reflection i -> n + 1 - i.

examples.code: G := DihedralGroup(4); #G; G.1*G.2; G.2^2; Order(G.1); G!(1, 3)(2, 4);

differs: Iterating over a dihedral group, and its subgroups and other structure (Center, Generators), are not supported yet.
A generator longer than a line is not printed (Magma wraps it).
DihedralGroup(3) is Sym(3), as in Magma; its reflection is (1, 2). G.-1 (an inverse by its index) is not supported yet.

name: Identity
summary: The identity element of a symmetric group.

name: Graph
summary: A graph on the vertices 1 .. n with the given edges (a constructor).
alternative: Sage mode's Graph, e.g. G = Graph({1: [2, 3], 2: [3]}), with is_connected(), connected_components(), shortest_path(), is_tree() and spanning_trees_count()
